import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mtick
import io

# Prepare the data
csv_data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type
Leica,2005,13.5,25600,324,811.8,Micro 4/3,1,E,Compact
Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR
"""

df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))

# Set a professional and clean style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="muted")

# Create the figure and axes
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 9))

# Create the bubble chart
# x-axis: megapixels, y-axis: price, size: max_iso, color: brand, style: body_type
scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='brand',
    size='max_iso',
    style='sensor_type',
    sizes=(200, 2500),  # Control the min and max size of bubbles
    alpha=0.8,
    edgecolor='black',
    linewidth=1.5,
    ax=ax
)

# --- Add annotations for clarity ---
for i in range(df.shape[0]):
    # Get the data for the current point
    row = df.iloc[i]
    brand = row['brand']
    year = row['model_year']
    weight = row['weight_grams']
    
    # Create the annotation text
    annotation_text = f"{brand} ({year})\n{weight}g"
    
    # Position the text
    ax.text(
        x=row['megapixels'],
        y=row['price_usd'] + 150,  # Offset text slightly above the bubble
        s=annotation_text,
        fontdict=dict(color='black', size=10, ha='center')
    )

# --- Customize the plot for impact and readability ---

# Set title and labels
ax.set_title('Camera Feature Comparison: Price vs. Megapixels', fontsize=20, weight='bold', pad=25)
ax.set_xlabel('Megapixels (MP)', fontsize=14, weight='bold', labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=14, weight='bold', labelpad=15)

# Format y-axis to show as currency
formatter = mtick.StrMethodFormatter('${x:,.0f}')
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(formatter)

# Adjust tick label size
ax.tick_params(axis='both', which='major', labelsize=12)

# Customize the grid
ax.grid(True, which='both', linestyle='--', linewidth=0.5)

# Move legend outside the plot to prevent overlap and organize it
handles, labels = ax.get_legend_handles_labels()
# Separate the legends for better clarity
brand_legend_idx = labels.index('brand')
max_iso_legend_idx = labels.index('max_iso')
sensor_type_legend_idx = labels.index('sensor_type')

legend1 = ax.legend(handles[brand_legend_idx+1:max_iso_legend_idx], labels[brand_legend_idx+1:max_iso_legend_idx], bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc='upper left', title='Brand', title_fontsize='13')
legend2 = ax.legend(handles[max_iso_legend_idx+1:sensor_type_legend_idx], labels[max_iso_legend_idx+1:sensor_type_legend_idx], bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.7), loc='upper left', title='Max ISO', title_fontsize='13')
legend3 = ax.legend(handles[sensor_type_legend_idx+1:], labels[sensor_type_legend_idx+1:], bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.4), loc='upper left', title='Sensor Type', title_fontsize='13')
ax.add_artist(legend1)
ax.add_artist(legend2)


# Ensure layout is tight and clean, making space for the legend
fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.85, 1])

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')

plt.close(fig)
